nodes.name: Microelectrode Fabrication and Polishing
nodes.procedure: The platinum microelectrode was prepared by sealing platinum wire (100 μm, 99.99%, Goodfellow) in a soda-lime glass capillary (1.4 mm outside diameter, 1.12 mm inside diameter, Hilgenberg) with a butane torch. The prepared polycrystalline platinum microelectrode was first polished with diamond polishing suspensions of decreasing particle size (3, 1, 0.25, 0.05 μm, Buehler) on micropolishing cloths and then polished with sandpaper (P2000, Starcke). Between each polishing process, the electrode was sonicated in Milli-Q water to remove any residual impurities.

nodes.name: Cell and Window Cleaning
nodes.procedure: The electrochemical cell and glass window were stored in permanganate solution (0.5 M H2SO4 and 1 g/L KMnO4). Before the experiment, any residual KMnO4 and MnO2 were removed by dipping them in a diluted piranha solution. Then, the electrochemical cell and glass window were cleaned by boiling them five times in Milli-Q water.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-speed optical imaging (3,000 f.p.s.) determined that bubble growth follows a power law R ∝ t^1/3, consistent with reaction-limited growth, and identified a bubble carpet thickness (δ) of 19-25 μm in HCl, HNO3, and HClO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A high-speed camera (Photron Fastcam Nova S16; frame rate, 3,000 f.p.s.) ... the radius evolution approximately follows a power law in time R ∝ t^x, with the exponent x close to 1/3 ... in HCl, HNO3 and HClO4, δ increases monotonically ... reaching values of 19–25 μm.
